description: Mechanical sympathy for the host and the services on it: which resource is busy or saturated, and who is responsible. The original hang forensics are the collapsed row at the bottom.

links.title: Process Exporter Docs
links.tooltip: Process exporter documentation and metrics reference

panels.description: Share of all cores doing work (100% minus idle), 5m average. Orange from 70%, red from 90%. Busy is not a problem on its own — check CPU WAIT next to it.
panels.title: CPU

panels.description: PSI: share of time at least one runnable task was waiting for a CPU, 5m average. Orange from 10%, red from 25%. Rising pressure means work is queueing — see who is using the CPU below.
panels.title: CPU WAIT

panels.description: Memory in use that the kernel cannot simply drop (100% minus MemAvailable). Orange from 80%, red from 90%. Page cache does not count — it is reclaimed on demand.
panels.title: MEMORY

panels.description: PSI: share of time at least one task was stalled on memory (reclaim, swap-in, refaults), 5m average. Orange from 5%, red from 20%. This is the early warning before OOM moves.
panels.title: MEM WAIT

panels.description: The busiest block device: share of time it had I/O in flight, 5m average. Orange from 60%, red from 90%. For an SSD, busy is not saturated — IO WAIT says whether anyone waited.
panels.title: DISK

panels.description: PSI: share of time at least one task was stalled waiting on block I/O, 5m average. Orange from 10%, red from 30%. High here with low DISK usually means one slow device (e.g. a USB or NTFS mount) rather than a saturated disk.
panels.title: IO WAIT

panels.description: Free space on the fullest real filesystem. Red under 10%, orange under 20% — SQLite, Prometheus and container logs all fail writes when their filesystem fills. The Disk band below says which filesystem.
panels.title: DISK FREE

panels.description: Processes the kernel killed for lack of memory over the selected time range (node_vmstat_oom_kill). Any is red: something was killed, and if it was a service, RESTARTS on the file_host dashboard moved too.
panels.title: OOM

panels.description: Whether Prometheus can scrape each collector this dashboard reads. A DOWN one turns its panels grey ("no data"), not green.
panels.title: Collectors

panels.description: Process CPU (process-exporter, summed over every group) as a share of the CPU the host actually spent (node_exporter). Normally somewhat under 100% — kernel threads are not matched. Red above 120%: the process collector is counting CPU the host never spent, so the per-process bars below overstate it.
panels.title: CPU ACCOUNTED

panels.description: The machine these percentages are of: logical CPUs, and total memory.
panels.title: CORES · RAM
CPU — who is using it, and who is waiting

panels.description: CPU per process group as a share of the whole machine (all cores), 5m average. Groups are process names (comm, 15 characters — hence ".gnome-shell-wr"). If CPU ACCOUNTED is red, these overstate.
panels.title: Who is using the CPU — processes

panels.description: CPU each container is using as a share of its own compose `cpus:` limit. Near 100% it is being throttled (next panel) — its requests wait for CPU even when the host is idle. Containers without a limit are not shown.

targets.expr: topk(10, 100 * sum by (name) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{name=~"$container"}[5m])) / on(name) (max by (name) (container_spec_cpu_quota{name=~"$container"}) / max by (name) (container_spec_cpu_period{name=~"$container"})))

panels.title: Who is hitting their limit — containers

panels.description: Utilisation (busy) against saturation (PSI: some task waiting for a CPU). The gap between them is the story: busy and not waiting is a well-used machine; waiting at modest busy is a queue.
panels.title: CPU — busy vs waiting

panels.description: For every container with a CPU limit: the share of scheduler periods in which it wanted more CPU than its limit and was paused. Anything sustained above a few percent is latency the service pays for its limit, independent of how busy the host is.
panels.title: Throttled — share of CPU periods each container was held back

panels.description: High load + low CPU = I/O bound bottleneck
panels.title: 📊 LOAD vs CPU DIVERGENCE

panels.description: Resident memory (RSS) per process group. Shared pages count once per process, so a group of many processes (browsers) overstates a little.
panels.title: Who is using memory — processes

panels.description: Working-set memory as a share of each container's compose `mem_limit`. At 100% the kernel OOM-kills it. Containers without a limit are not shown.
panels.title: Who is near their limit — containers

panels.description: Used memory (excluding reclaimable cache), swap in use, and memory PSI. Swap climbing while pressure stays flat is harmless parking of cold pages; both climbing together is thrashing.
panels.title: Memory — used vs stalled
Disk — who is filling and hitting it

panels.description: How full each real filesystem is. Orange from 80%, red from 90%.
panels.title: Disk space — % used per filesystem

panels.description: Storage bytes read plus written per second per process group, 5m average (/proc/<pid>/io — network traffic is not included).
panels.title: Who is doing disk I/O — processes

panels.description: Per device: share of time busy, and the average time an I/O took (await). IO PSI is the host-wide share of time some task waited on I/O. Await climbing on one device is the slow disk; PSI says whether anyone felt it.
panels.title: Disk — busy, waiting, and how slow

panels.description: High load average + Low CPU usage = I/O bound hang

targets.expr:
(
  (node_load1 / count without(cpu, mode) (node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle"})) > bool 3
)
*
(
  (100 - avg without(cpu, mode) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle"}[5m])) * 100) < bool 30
)
